95179.subject: Botany
95179.text: Which of the following tissue is absent in vascular bundles of monocot stem?
95179.sol: Monocot stems have most of their vascular bundles near the outside edge of the stem. The bundles are surrounded by large parenchyma in the cortex region. There is no pith region in monocots. In dicot stems, bundles are present in a ring surrounding parenchyma cells in a pith region.

96277.subject: Botany
96277.text: Enzyme recombinase has a significant role during the gamete formation. In which phase is it active?
96277.sol: The crossing over process occurring in the meiotic division is a enzyme mediated process. The enzyme involved is recombinase participates in the process of crossing over during the pachytene phase of prophase -I.

96368.subject: Botany
96368.text: Which of the following holds true for the pachytene stage of meiotic cell division?
options: This stage leads to genetic recombination, hence variations in sexually reproducing organisms.
In this stage, the process of exchange of genetic material between sister chromatids of non- homologous chromo
This stage takes place only in haploid cells of the body eg. Gametes
96368.sol: The meiotic cell division comprises two successive nuclear division the meiosis I and meiosis II. The meiosis I have four stages prophase I, metaphase 1, anaphase 1, and telophase 1. The prophase I have further been divided into five phases depending on the chromosomal behavior. The pachytene is the third phase of the five phases where the four chromatids appear as tetrads. Crossing over between two homologous chromosomes takes place during this phase and therefore leads to the recombination of the genetic material

96683.subject: Botany
96683.text: Which one of the following organisms has a role in converting ammonia into nitrites?
96683.sol: Ammonia is converted into nitrate by nitrifying activities of bacteria, this process is called nitrification. Soil bacteria such as Nitrosomonas and Nitrosococcus convert ammonia to nitrite. N H 3 + 3 O 2 → 2 H N O 2 + 2 H 2 O

96801.subject: Botany
96801.text: Which process results in decrease of nitrogen content in soil?
96801.sol: The bacteria which carry out denitrification are called denitrifying bacteria, like Thiobacillus denitrificans, Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Micrococcus denitrificans also occur in the soil which converts the nitrate and ammonia into atmospheric free elemental nitrogen. The process in which molecular nitrogen is released back into the atmosphere by reduction of nitrate present in the soil is called denitrification.

97032.subject: Botany
97032.text: Identify the correct order where plants show alternate, opposite, and whorled phyllotaxy respectively:
97032.sol: In alternate phyllotaxy, only a single leaf develops from each node as in China rose. In opposite phyllotaxy, two leaves develop from each node as in Calotropis and Guava. In whorled phyllotaxy, more than two leaves develop from each node as in Nerium and Alstonia.

97237.subject: Botany

Promotion of male flowers in cucumbers thereby increasing its yield
Breaking the bud dormancy and promoting sprouting of potato tubers
Promotion of root growth and root hair formation, thus helping the plants to increase their absorption surface

98151.sol: Glycogen is the main storage polysaccharide in animals. Hence, it is commonly called 'animal starch'. Blue-green algae and fungi also store glycogen as 'fuel reserve'.
